The varying widths of the confidence intervals directly reflect the escalating uncertainty as the forecast horizon extends. This interval significantly broadens for the 1-week forecast (77.69 to 84.47), and even more so for the 1-month period (74.39 to 87.91). This widening is driven by several sources of uncertainty, including the inherent unpredictability of the future, the potential for compounding effects of small daily fluctuations, and the increased likelihood of unforeseen external events influencing the outcome as time progresses.

While my confidence intervals cover 90% of expected outcomes, there are specific, high-impact risks that could push the actual results beyond these stated ranges. These typically involve unforeseen "black swan" events or significant systemic shocks not easily captured by standard probabilistic models. Examples could include sudden and drastic policy changes relevant to the forecasted metric, major geopolitical upheavals, rapid technological disruptions, or severe economic downturns or booms that fundamentally alter the underlying conditions faster or more profoundly than anticipated. Such events, while low probability, possess the potential to cause outcomes to deviate dramatically from even the widest parts of my forecasted range.
